conviction_note: Sum of five findings nets to +1.2: two IBEX-specific, well-dated positives (an unprecedented new-country capacity commitment 8 days before the FY2027 guide, and a peso that has moved ~10% in IBEX's favour and keeps going) against three softer negatives (peer deterioration that is already sector narrative, a pre-flagged GAAP impairment, and a routine-looking COO Form 144); with no usable option chain, a 5-up/0-down reaction history and a consensus target that equals spot, I have a mild positive tilt and nothing that justifies a large number.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-02, eight days before the fiscal-year-end print and the FY2027 guidance introduction, ibex announced its first-ever entry into Egypt - a Cairo (City Stars, Nasr City) delivery centre opening in October and scaling to 1,000 employees in nine months, serving HealthTech, Technology and Retail clients - a ~3% addition to a 36,000-person workforce in a country it has never operated in.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a GlobeNewswire site-expansion release with no dollar figure attached, on a stock that trades 99k shares a day and that stockanalysis.com shows as covered by two estimating analysts whose price targets were last updated 2026-05-07 - i.e. nobody has re-cut a model since the announcement. If the market had read a brand-new offshore country plus a signed lease and live hiring as a statement about contracted FY2027 demand, the 20-day run-up would be more than +6.5%, the consensus target would not still be $37.50 against a $37.40 spot, and someone would have written it up. Companies do not commit capex and 1,000 hires into a geography with no existing client base a week before setting annual guidance unless the demand behind it is already signed.
findings.independence: Second, separate capacity commitment three weeks earlier: on 2026-08-10 ibex said it would hire 400 more in Tegucigalpa by year-end off a ~1,200 base, with the Honduran president publicly discussing doubling or tripling the workforce - https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/10/3341871/0/en/ibex-ceo-and-honduras-president-nasry-asfura-meet-to-discuss-growth-investment-and-ongoing-partnership.html . Corroborating direction from a third source: management raised FY2026 capex guidance to $25-30M from $20-25M 'to meet increased demand in higher-margin regions' on the 2026-05-06 call.

findings.finding: USD/PHP stands at 62.63 on 2026-09-10, up 9.6% over twelve months, and averaged near 60 through IBEX's April-June quarter against roughly 57 a year earlier - a direct cost-side tailwind for a company whose offshore delivery (Philippines, Pakistan, India) produced 51.1% of nine-month FY2026 revenue and which runs eight of its ~29 delivery sites in the Philippines.
findings.why_not_priced: The FY2027 EBITDA-margin guide is set against a hedge book that rolls onto a 62-peso rate, versus the ~56-58 embedded in FY2026. With two estimating analysts and no published revision since 2026-05-07, there is no visible model carrying a re-based FY2027 margin. If it were priced you would see an FY2027 margin whisper above the 12.8-13.1% FY2026 guided rate and a target above spot; instead the consensus target is $37.50 on a $37.40 stock. The offset - IBEX hedges forward, so the FY2026 quarter itself captures less of this than the raw rate implies - is exactly why the payload sits in the FY2027 guide rather than the printed quarter.
findings.independence: Delivery-location revenue mix (offshore 51.1% of the nine months to 2026-03-31) comes from a different document, the Q3 FY2026 10-Q: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001720420/000172042026000011/ibex-20260331.htm . Site counts by country from Nearshore Americas: https://nearshoreamericas.com/ibex-is-losing-steam-in-its-nearshore-ops/

findings.finding: Both listed pure-play peers reported IBEX's exact April-June calendar quarter after IBEX last spoke on 2026-05-06 and both deteriorated: Concentrix cut full-year revenue guidance on 2026-06-29 and fell ~22% after hours citing accelerating offshoring headwinds and client spending pressure, and TTEC reported Q2 revenue down 11.3% year-on-year on 2026-08-11.
findings.why_not_priced: IBEX has traded up 6.46% over 20 days and sits 11% off its 52-week high with put/call open interest of 0.10 on 549 total contracts - nobody is hedged and the tape shows no mark-to-peer at all. If the market had discounted the peer set into IBEX's FY2027 guide you would see at least one of the eight covering analysts cut a target since June; stockanalysis.com shows the last target change on 2026-05-07. I size this small deliberately: the mechanism hurting Concentrix (clients pushing work offshore) is the mechanism IBEX profits from - IBEX is 51% offshore and has grown 16-17% for five straight quarters while these two shrank - so the read-through is directionally weak, and the brief is right that the generic AI-disruption narrative is already in every sector note.
findings.independence: TTEC, a separate company and a separate filing: Q2 2026 revenue $455M, -11.3% y/y, reported 2026-08-11 - https://www.stocktitan.net/news/TTEC/ttec-announces-second-quarter-2026-financial-086wpd8ys0vk.html

findings.finding: On the 2026-05-06 call the CFO pre-announced that Q4 FY2026 - the quarter about to be reported - will carry an additional asset impairment charge as the company adjusts capacity following a client's shift of volumes out of nearshore into offshore, on top of $0.8M of Q3 severance; nearshore was 23.3% of nine-month revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: It was one sentence of CFO commentary on a call for a company with two estimating analysts; it produced no 8-K, no press release, and no target revision (last change 2026-05-07). If it were priced the GAAP-versus-adjusted gap in the FY2026 estimate would be visible and at least one note would have flagged shrinking nearshore capacity into the FY2027 guide. I keep it small because the charge is non-cash and will be adjusted out of the EPS the market actually trades - the residual risk is that a headline GAAP loss line and a written-down nearshore footprint frame the FY2027 revenue guide as mix-deflationary.
findings.independence: Nearshore's 23.3% share of nine-month revenue and the delivery-mix disaggregation come from the 10-Q, a different document: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001720420/000172042026000011/ibex-20260331.htm . Longer-run nearshore contraction independently documented by Nearshore Americas: https://nearshoreamericas.com/ibex-is-losing-steam-in-its-nearshore-ops/

findings.finding: COO David Afdahl filed a Form 144 on 2026-09-08 - two days before the fiscal-year-end print - to sell 17,500 shares worth $649,008 through RBC, and the filing reports nothing sold in the preceding three months.
findings.why_not_priced: Form 144s are not carried by the news aggregators that cover this name and the corresponding Form 4 was not on EDGAR as of 2026-09-10, so the transaction is invisible to anyone not reading the raw filing index. If it were priced the 5-day run-up would not be the only sign of pressure and the sale would have appeared in the insider-trading trackers that carried every earlier IBEX Form 4. The honest discount: IBEX insiders sell constantly - eleven open-market sales and zero purchases in the last six months - so the base rate strips most of the signal out, and 17,500 shares is under a fifth of a day's volume.
findings.independence: The 11-sales/0-purchases six-month insider record is from a different source: https://www.secform4.com/insider-trading/1720420.htm . Note this finding rests on a single primary document; treat it as one source.

searched_and_found_nothing: Identity of the largest client (10% of nine-month revenue) and of the 'one of the largest payers in the world' driving 53.7% HealthTech growth - the 10-K and 10-Q name no clients, and I could not tie IBEX to any named payer's own disclosure, so the client-concentration door in the sweep row produced nothing checkable

The Amazon warrant (1,674,017 granted 2017-11-13, 1,171,812 vested on milestones through 2024-06-30, all unexercised) - a real dilution overhang but static, already in the 14.994M diluted count, and unchanged since FY2024

Buyback denominator: the sweep row's premise that IBEX is still shrinking the count aggressively does not hold - FY2025's 3.9M shares was dominated by the one-off TRGI block; ordinary-course buying was only 310,158 shares/$10.1M in nine months of FY2026 and the new authorisation announced 2026-05-13 is $20M over 12 months (~4% of cap). All of it is in the 8-K and the 10-Q, so there is no staleness to exploit

Pakistan operational disruption in the April-June window - the 2026 internet-shutdown episodes I found were maintenance (April) and Kashmir/Islamabad-specific, and BPOs were explicitly exempted from the Islamabad lockdown; no IBEX-relevant outage

Third-party headcount data (Revelio Labs shows 31,977 and -3.3% y/y) flatly contradicts the company's own 33,000 (FY2025 10-K) to 36,000+ (2026-08-27) - LinkedIn-derived counts are unreliable for offshore agent populations, so I discarded it rather than build on a number I could not reconcile
Baird fireside chat of 2026-06-02: no transcript or webcast recording reachable, so no post-Q3 management framing of FY2027 beyond the May call
American Century's 13G/A (event date 2026-06-30, 3.8% of class) implies a drop below 5%, but with no prior-amendment figure on the face of the filing I could not size the distribution
investors.ibex.co returned 503 on every attempt; the news list was reconstructed from stocktitan and GlobeNewswire instead
Job-posting counts on careers.ibex.co - the site does not expose a req count
baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with (the chain is unusable, 549 contracts, put/call OI 0.10), so the only priced statement available is the +6.46% 20-day run-up and a $37.50 consensus target sitting on a $37.40 spot - and my net tilt cuts mildly with the run-up rather than against it, which is uncomfortable given the stock has already re-rated ~78% off its low and has never fallen materially on any of its last seven prints.
